contract_projection.summary: Source radial state initialization in the explicit TokaGrad compatibility development variant; defaults and original failure semantics retained.

assumptions: Source-admissible selected reduced analytic configuration.
Stateful calls require genuine source predecessor and geometry-history ownership.
This compatibility contract does not establish scientific correctness.

identity.coordinates: cell-centered thermal/density fields and selected face current grid
identity.definition: Construct source profiles and current convention; obtain reduced geometry; bind Phi_b and dV/drho to the initial history fields. Source initial-current selectors and fixed bounded current/geometry updates remain unchanged.
identity.direction: Declared input fields/configuration to returned coordinate/profile/state fields.
identity.geometry: Reduced fixed-boundary tokamak for state mappings; radial coordinate only for grid mappings.
identity.model: Initialization heuristics, not an equilibrium/transport solution.

stored-energy update.  It can be smaller than ``sim.dt`` when tau_E is
short, so downstream history/plot/optimization code should accumulate this
value rather than assuming a uniform ``i * sim.dt`` time grid.

transport interface only carries a scalar density diffusivity ``Dn``.

apis.signature: chang_hinton_neoclassical_diffusivities(rho, Te, Ti, ne20, q, machine, sim, eq=None)
apis.source_docstring:
Reduced positive scalar neoclassical diffusivities [m^2/s].

The ion heat channel uses the common Chang-Hinton all-collisionality fit,
written as a positive scalar diffusivity proportional to
``q^2 rho_i^2 nu_ii / epsilon^(3/2)`` with banana/plateau/Pfirsch-Schlueter
interpolation terms [C. S. Chang and F. L. Hinton, Phys. Fluids 25, 1493
(1982)].  This avoids the sign-indefinite scalar projection of the full
Angioni-Sauter flux-force matrix and is intended as a robust analytic
comparison model.

Electron heat and particle channels are reduced random-walk estimates using
the same collisionality interpolation scale.  They are positive by
construction and deliberately simple; tune ``neoclassical_chi_scale`` and
``neoclassical_D_scale`` when matching a higher-fidelity neoclassical code.
